questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the school, local language, wheater, city life and the possibility of traveling.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was one of the best decisions I have ever made and I would do it all over!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Pretty difficult.
To travel to Singapore you have to fill out a lot of paperwork and there is a lot of bureaucracy in total so it would have been nice if there was a better checklist before arriving of what we had to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a few emails and that about it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: People were very nice overall but it was a little difficult to get to now where I had to be for classes and to fill out the last information to get my student card, long-term visa etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Student halls however most danish students didn't get housing
I lived at Eusoff Hall which had its both positives and negatives.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were included in the stay at Eusoff Hall. The meal plan had dinner six times a week and breakfast 5 times a week. There were a few selections every night/morning but nothing special.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is not necessarily updated rooms you get located in. The halls are very different from where you stay—both with the quality/size of the bed and the state of the room. My room didn't have air-conditioning which is a must in Singapore due to the high temperatures and humidity. Students have to be careful with their clothes in Singapore if they are not located in a room with AC due to their clothes molding. Furthermore, do students need to know that the sound level is relatively high In the halls due to students going to very late sleep so I didn't sleep very much on my exchange stay - I probably slept around 5 hours every night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would really recommend a room with AC and do your due diligence before choosing. My room was located close to my lecture and classrooms which was nice. Also, it was fun being a part of a sports hall where I had the possibility to do different sports. It was also lovely living with many locals and not only other exchange students even though I spend by far most of my time with other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: More detailed information could have been provided to know where I had to be and show up.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Was difficult to get to know where I had to be so in the future it would be nice if more information was provided.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot - I mostly consulted with other exchange students and got a little help from the locals at my hall.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registration for classes was pretty easy however I only got three classes at the beginning and I had to have four to get up to the 30 ects I needed. So I registered for one more a few weeks after I arrived and that was fairly easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just wish for as many classes as possible at the start and then switch classes when you arrive because it is very easy to try out multiple classes in the beginning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I liked it overall.
The level was pretty similar to Denmark but I had less schoolwork in Singapore which was nice because it also gave me time to have fun while I was there.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four classes: International Trade 1, International Finance 1, Game Theory, and Money & Banking. All classes were well-leveled and on the same level as in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty similar but with less tutorial work. The tutorial work however was more included with grades depending on participation, assignments and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Trade 1, International Finance 1, Game Theory, and Money & Banking

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend International Trade 1, International Finance 1, and Game Theory.
Money & Banking didn't really have the same level.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I only had to buy a new computer as unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and transportation were cheaper than expected. Everything else was around the same prices as in Copenhagen with alcohol being very expensive in Singapore.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was part of multiple sports with my hall. I played football, pickleball, squash, and more. It was a lot of fun and NUS sports facilities were very very good. They were up to date and I had the possibility to play every sport I could think of. The hall also gave possibilities to be part of a theatre, music bands, and more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The central part of the Campus (U-town) had many offerings every single week. Everything you could think of they had. It was a lot of fun being part of that because it is very different from Denmark.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports team. It is a good way to meet locals and other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Singapore is very well located to go on holidays on the weekends. We traveled to Bali, Seoul and Kuala Lumpur having a lot of fun doing so.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. Singapore is different in many ways but also very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sports or other cultural events. Else join a hall.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Locals in Singapore study more than in Denmark, but as an exchange student I spend most of my time with other exchange students and we had a lot of time to have fun.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Be social and join sports or other cultural events. Then also walk around the city with locals or other exchange students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go into it open-mindedly. In Singapore, you will spend a lot of time with other exchange students in the same position as you so you have to socialize. 
Be prepared with documents. Singapore has a bit of Bureaucracy so you have to have patience.
Pack well. Singapore is very warm and humid so only bring summer clothes with a few hoodies and pants for the very cooled air-conditioned lecture halls.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk with UCPH about if there are other exchange students going from KU because it helps a lot talking with others about all the practical things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from around the world and making long-lasting friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting everything practical ready when arriving in Singapore.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun! You will have the greatest time of your life. Be patient with all of the practical things because it will all be worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
